summary.headline: Praveg Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.7% to INR43.75 crore but EBITDA turned negative at INR2.94 crore (-6.64% margin), with net loss of INR20.13 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR43.75 crore, up 16.70% YoY, with hospitality and events at INR27.73 crore and advertising at INR16.02 crore. Q2 EBITDA was negative INR2.94 crore (margin -6.64%), and H1 EBITDA was INR0.97 crore (1.06% margin) on H1 revenue of INR90.46 crore. Management attributed the margin pressure to seasonal monsoon weakness, GST-related reversal of input credit under dynamic pricing for rooms below INR7,500, and higher employee costs from labour law changes. The Lakshadweep Praveg Atoll resort (100 rooms) opened on October 21, 2026, and management guided to stronger Q3 and Q4 driven by festivals, weddings, MICE and events.

financial_highlights.change: +16.70% YoY vs INR37.60 crore in Q2 FY26
Q2 FY26 EBITDA was positive around INR4 crore per analyst question; company did not dispute
up INR16.17 crore over H1 FY26

segments.name: Hospitality and events
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR27.73 crore; H1 FY27 INR57.53 crore. Portfolio about 927 rooms across 17 resorts and one 5-star hotel; Q2 is seasonally weakest due to monsoon.

segments.name: Advertising (Abhik Advertising, Bidhan Advertising and Marketing; 51% stake)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR16.02 crore; H1 FY27 INR32.22 crore. Management cited advertising revenue of INR34 crore in FY25 and INR56 crore in FY26, and expects similar incremental growth in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Top line expected to be higher than last year in Q3 and Q4, with sizeable growth in advertising.

Event and exhibition revenue expected in Q3: about INR13-14 crore from one just-concluded event (Bharat Parv, inaugurated October 31, 2026) plus 2-3 further projects; Q2 events were only INR5-6 crore.
Around INR10 crore wedding business expected from Adalaj this quarter and the next; 10-15 weddings expected at Kevadiya colony vs 1-2 last year.
EBITDA for the full year expected to turn positive at 25-30% margin per management, but no time frame given for PAT breakeven; Lakshadweep ramp-up and flight connectivity are key drivers.
Occupancy and ARR expected to rise in Q3 and Q4 with festival season, winter season, weddings and Lakshadweep opening.
capex_capacity: Praveg Atoll Thinnakara Island, Lakshadweep, commenced operations October 21, 2026: 100 rooms (85 cocoon-shaped, 15 shell-shaped), conference hall for up to 400 guests.
Asset-light semi-permanent structures cost about INR60-75 lakh per room vs INR1.25-1.5 crore per room for civil structure hotels, per management.
Management cited about INR300-400 crore invested in capital assets (land rights and leases not owned); company owns the structures on leased land.
Meghalaya: 30-year concession for a luxury cottage project, 40 rooms, total outlay INR25-30 crore; lease right in hand.
Alibaug (2 properties) and Kashid land acquired with legal clearance ongoing; one Rajasthan acquisition pending; Tanzania (Serengeti forest) land allocated and development started.
Bangaram (Lakshadweep) run by IHCL under its Selection brand has about 50 rooms operational; management noted 150 rooms in total at Lakshadweep (Bangaram 50 plus Thinnakara 100).
demand_pricing: Management said demand is mostly domestic and bookings have not been affected by rising ATF prices or airfares; no cancellations were reported.
Dynamic pricing introduced after late-September GST rule change: for room rates below INR7,500, input credit must be proportionately reversed, which hit P&L.
Management said occupancy and ARR are trending upward across properties, and Lakshadweep ARR is higher than the company average.
Breakeven benchmarks given by management: 30-40% occupancy for breakeven; 40-55% for 20-25% EBITDA margin; 65-75% for 40%+ EBITDA margin.
Wedding bookings for peak dates said to be almost fully committed at Grand Eulogia, Adalaj, Statue of Unity and Kachigam.
Statue of Unity contingent contract worth about INR11.16 crore plus GST (letter of acceptance from Tourism Corporation of Gujarat) for October 20 to November 1, 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA decline YoY, and is demand shifting between premium, mid-market and budget segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the GST dynamic-pricing reversal of input credit for rooms under INR7,500 and higher employee costs from labour law changes, with opex as a percentage of sales broadly stable. No shift in demand across segments was reported; occupancy rising at all properties.

qa_highlights.question: Did depreciation (up about 30%) and interest (up about 57%) rise due to leases or borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no additional borrowings; the depreciation step-up reflects full-quarter effect of properties, and depreciation was flat in Q2 vs Q2 FY26 per management.

qa_highlights.question: When will PAT turn positive, and how much of the Q2 loss is seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business must be judged on full-year numbers, expects EBITDA margin of 25-30% for the full year, and linked PAT recovery to Lakshadweep occupancy and ARR once flight connectivity improves. No specific PAT breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the portfolio is asset-light, and will new partnership models extend to upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all properties follow the asset-light model; the company owns structures on leased land and rent is fixed regardless of occupancy. Meghalaya, Alibaug and Kashid are in the pipeline on the same model.

qa_highlights.question: Which properties are underutilised and will occupancy data be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Diu, Daman and Jawai run at good occupancy; Tent City Narmada and Ayodhya are below average due to seasonality. Management agreed to disclose property-level occupancy and region-wise performance from the next call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the year and next 1-2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top line will be higher than last year; advertising is expected to grow well and event revenue is hard to predict as it depends on last-minute government events. EBITDA depends on Lakshadweep ramp-up and depreciation on new properties.

risks_watch: Q2 EBITDA is negative and H1 EBITDA is only INR0.97 crore; full-year EBITDA recovery depends on Q3-Q4 event, wedding and Lakshadweep ramp-up.
Fixed land rent payable regardless of occupancy, which amplifies seasonal margin swings.
GST dynamic-pricing input-credit reversal for rooms below INR7,500 and labour-law employee cost increases are ongoing cost pressures.
Lakshadweep ramp-up is constrained by flight connectivity; management is working with the government.
Event and exhibition revenue is hard to forecast because events are often booked at short notice.
Net loss of INR33.37 crore in H1 and rising depreciation and interest costs; no PAT breakeven timeline given.
Next quarter: check property-level occupancy disclosure, Q3 event revenue (about INR13-14 crore from Bharat Parv) and Lakshadweep occupancy.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q3-Q4 seasonal recovery, events, weddings and advertising, but defensive on Q2 losses and PAT timing, which management attributed to seasonality, GST and labour cost changes. Answers on profitability timelines and some property details were general rather than quantified.

growth.why: Management guides top line above last year in Q3 and Q4 with sizeable advertising growth, backed by specific items (Bharat Parv event INR13-14 crore in Q3, ~INR10 crore Adalaj weddings, Statue of Unity contract INR11.16 crore plus GST, Lakshadweep Atoll 100 rooms live), but no revenue growth % is quantified and EBITDA turnaround to 25-30% margin has no timeline.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides full-year EBITDA margin of 25-30% after H1 at 1.06% and Q2 at -6.64%, leaning on Q3-Q4 events, weddings and Lakshadweep ramp-up, though no quarterly path was given and GST and labour cost headwinds persist.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Praveg Atoll Thinnakara (100 rooms) commenced operations October 21, 2026, and Meghalaya's 40-room project has a lease right in hand, with Alibaug, Kashid and Tanzania land in progress.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides top line above last year in Q3 and Q4 and H1 room nights rose to 55,925 from 44,959 (+24%), backed by INR13-14 crore Bharat Parv event revenue in Q3 and 10-15 Kevadiya weddings vs 1-2 last year, though no volume % is quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management cites INR300-400 crore already invested and a pipeline (Meghalaya, Alibaug, Kashid, Rajasthan, Tanzania) but no new capex amount or timing was announced and utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is qualitative (top line 'always better than last year', no growth % quantified) and EBITDA is negative in Q2 with H1 at 1.06%, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Full-year 25-30% EBITDA margin needs a very strong H2 from H1 at 1.06%, and event revenue is hard to forecast (Q2 events only INR5-6 crore), while flight connectivity constrains Lakshadweep ramp-up.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new brand or product launch was discussed beyond the Lakshadweep Atoll opening already under way.

rows.label: Statue of Unity contingent contract INR11.16 crore plus GST
rows.why: Letter of acceptance from Tourism Corporation of Gujarat is in hand for INR11.16 crore plus GST, covering the October 20 to November 1, 2026 window.

rows.label: Adalaj wedding business about INR10 crore
rows.why: Management expects around INR10 crore of wedding revenue from Adalaj across this quarter and the next, with peak dates almost fully committed.

rows.label: Advertising growth FY27 at FY26 incremental pace
rows.why: Advertising was INR34 crore in FY25 and INR56 crore in FY26, and H1 FY27 reached INR32.22 crore, with management expecting the same incremental growth this year.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q3-Q4 events, weddings, advertising and the Lakshadweep opening, but defensive on Q2 losses and PAT timing, which it put down to monsoon seasonality, GST input-credit reversal and labour costs.
